data.title: The Open Crossing
data.text:
At the beginning, you passed the bolted stone and the survey hut at Vell Foot; both remained intact. Later, the field cabin above the third falls was destroyed. I keep those entries together: the old route and its measurements, then the place where Tomas Lind worked above them.

At Upper Vell, the dam went. Anna Sorel’s handover note says it was designed in six weeks and built in eleven months, for the lake as surveyed in March 2029. It would not hold a larger one. The fjord chapel was destroyed; its notice board directed anyone looking for a name to the lists at the church hall. Tomas Lind’s chalet still stands, kettles and all. So does the village lift. I have put those records beside what the water took.

The valley’s decisions came from different desks, with different reach. A hurried dam was built; the Ministry’s old letter and its new spillway programme share a letterhead. The second Alpine Pass crossing, unfunded for eighteen years, is now approved. An approved page is only quiet until someone builds it.

Your river reached the sea. Tomas’s letter asks for a new stake line, higher up, where the ice still is. I have left that request open on the page. You cannot undo the river behind you. You can still decide where it goes next.
